subject: Privileged credentials & IAM / audit logging — remediation status and evidence
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@penprobe.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security <acme-security@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PenTest excerpt: exposed API keys, audit gaps, and overly-broad IAM — request for scope/ETAs

Hi Priyom,

We ran the initial external penetration test for Acme Logistics last week and wanted to surface three findings that need quick attention and confirmation of scope:

1) Exposed API keys found in a public S3 index (Finding 4) — appears to be keys used by an integration service account.
2) Service-account activity not present in audit logs for the timeframe of the access (Finding 7) — we cannot see service-to-service calls in your audit pipeline.
3) Overly-broad IAM role attached to a deployment role allowing iam:PassRole and broad storage permissions (Finding 11).

Attached is an excerpt (penprobe_excerpt_findings_4_7_11.pdf). Please confirm whether the integration mentioned in Finding 4 belongs to a third-party partner or an internal sys-integration. Also provide an ETA for evidence (proof-of-fix) for these findings: screenshots of rotated keys/config, log samples showing the service-account telemetry, and the diff/PR for IAM policy changes.

Our timeline: Acme needs initial evidence within 72 hours if possible; otherwise let us know a realistic date.

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Senior Consultant, PenProbe Ltd
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@penprobe.com>
Cc: Acme Security <acme-security@acme.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Mar 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PenTest excerpt: exposed API keys, audit gaps, and overly-broad IAM — request for scope/ETAs

Hi Lisa / Acme team,

Thanks for the heads up and the excerpt. Acknowledged — triage kicked off. Quick assignment:
- Mina will lead secrets rotation and verify scope for the key referenced in Finding 4.
- Karthik will own the IAM policy remediation (Finding 11) and will prepare the terraform diff/PR.
- Neha will validate the audit pipeline and provide log evidence for Finding 7.

Initial plan and target ETAs (we'll update if anything slips):
- Secrets rotation and evidence: 2025-03-20 EOD PDT
- IAM policy changes + PR: 2025-03-19 EOD PDT
- Audit pipeline evidence (sample logs + ingestion confirmation): 2025-03-20 EOD PDT

I'll publish proof artifacts to a secure drive and share links once available. Attaching the vendor excerpt (forwarded).

Regards,
Priyom Das
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference

--- Forwarded attachment: penprobe_excerpt_findings_4_7_11.pdf ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa@penprobe.com>, Acme Security <acme-security@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Mar 2025 11:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PenTest excerpt: exposed API keys, audit gaps, and overly-broad IAM — request for scope/ETAs

Quick technical update from infra:

Summary of actions completed/ongoing for Finding 11 (IAM):
- Identified the deployment role (redwood-deploy-prod) with iam:PassRole and storage full-access.
- Created an interim least-privilege policy that scopes storage to the exact prefix used by the service.
- Implemented policy change in terraform branch fix/iam-restrict-20250319 and raised PR #842.
- Running a canary rollout to 3 clusters; monitoring for permission errors.

ETA for full rollout and PoF (policy diff + PR link): 2025-03-19 18:00:00 PDT. Attached: iam-policy-diff-20250319.patch (excerpt).

Notes: We'll also add a guardrail to prevent iam:PassRole for machine roles unless explicitly required by the deployment definition. If Acme wants the PR link and a short walkthrough, we can share after the canary completes.

-Karthik
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Mar 18, 2025 at 09:12, Lisa Chen <lisa@penprobe.com> wrote:
> (original pen test excerpt attached)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@penprobe.com>, Acme Security <acme-security@acme.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 Mar 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PenTest excerpt: exposed API keys, audit gaps, and overly-broad IAM — request for scope/ETAs

Hi Lisa / Acme team,

Status update and evidence package (final):

1) Finding 4 — Exposed API key
- Action: Rotated the exposed keys and revoked any prior tokens tied to the integration service account.
- Evidence: key-rotation-log-20250320.csv attached (rotation timestamps, key IDs, owner tags).
- Scope confirmation: This was an internal integration (internal-svc-bridge), not a third-party partner. We have flagged the integration owner to validate downstream clients.

2) Finding 7 — Audit logging gap
- Action: Enabled enhanced service-account audit logging (service-to-service traces) and replayed historical ingestion for the affected window.
- Evidence: sample logs uploaded to secure drive (link below) with annotated timestamps showing service-account call IDs.

3) Finding 11 — IAM permissions
- Action: Applied least-privilege policy and removed broad storage access and unnecessary iam:PassRole from the deployment role. Canary rollout complete without errors.
- Evidence: iam-policy-diff-20250319.patch attached and PR #842 in infra repo.

Evidence links: https://drive.redwoodinternal.com/secure/evidence/ACME/penprobe-20250320
HubSpot ticket: HS-987654
Jira support case: JIRA-SUP-4321

Attachments: key-rotation-log-20250320.csv; iam-policy-diff-20250319.patch; penprobe_excerpt_findings_4_7_11.pdf

Next steps:
- Mina will run a secrets inventory sweep and provide a short report for any exposed credentials outside this finding (ETA 2025-03-22).
- Neha will produce a short technical note on audit retention and ingestion guarantees for Acme (ETA 2025-03-22).
- Priyom to coordinate validation with PenProbe for final sign-off and provide any additional artifacts they request.

Please confirm if Acme wants a scheduled walkthrough of the PR and logs; we can set up a 30-min session tomorrow.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
